HEAD is unchanged (d65316e, M4.13f) -- a moved HEAD would have moved the excluded-file hash too. THE ONLY NEW BYTES ARE ONE ADDED LINE, `rounds:M4.47` in baselines/review.txt. No test byte and no production byte moved, so every round-3 measurement carries and I did not re-run the mutations: re-measuring identical bytes would produce a number I already recorded, and reporting it as fresh would be the claim non-negotiable 4 forbids. NOTHING RE-CHECKED, BECAUSE NOTHING MOVED: the four round-2 fixes each still stand pinned by the mutant they were minted against (`landed.sequence() > 0` -> `> 1` reddens only LocalSequencerSealRaceTest#aCrossedEpochThatOnlyOPENEDIsStillTheAncestor; both forcings of the origin flag are dead, `true` reddening ChainReplayEmptyOriginTest#inheritedCROSSESAnEmptyOriginToReachTheOffsets and `false` reddening #replayDoesNOTCrossItsOWNEmptyChain; deleting `burned.recoverChainEnd()` reddens aRacingChainLONGERThanTheRedriveBudgetStillConverges with 'seal did not converge at seq 8 within 8 redrive(s)'), and check-mutants is a gate the packet reports PASSED against these exact staged bytes. ⚠️ ASKED TO CONFIRM THE COMMIT BODY'S SWEEP CLAIM IS NOT FLATTERING, AND I CANNOT READ THE COMMIT BODY -- .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG still holds M4.13f's message, so the M4.47 body is not in the tree and nothing I say binds it. Against the quoted text: 'four mutations are caught by unit tests and not by it' is exact (loop start `epoch - 1` -> `epoch - 2`; `break` after the first crossed epoch; dropping `prevEpoch = crossed`; `landed.sequence() > 1`), '0.645s' is exact, and 'rule-20 coverage of shapes the hand-built fixtures do not construct ... would catch the NEXT defect of this class rather than this one' is my framing, not a flattering one. ONE WORD IS STRONGER THAN WHAT I MEASURED: I recorded 'I could not find a mutant it uniquely kills' over an enumerated set of mutations, which is a search that came up empty, not a proof that no such mutant exists. 'UNIQUELY KILLS NO MUTANT' asserts the proof. I am not filing it -- no artifact in the tree makes that claim; the sweep's own javadoc (CommitProtocolSimulationTest.java:209-229) claims only measured regression evidence, 19 violating seeds and 119 I2 violations with the two ADR-0037 hunks reverted, which is the honest form -- but if the body states it, 'no unique kill found over the mutations enumerated here' is the sentence the measurement supports. The one added line's own testable claim checks out: seven new @Test methods in the staged diff (inheritedCROSSESAnEmptyOriginToReachTheOffsets, replayDoesNOTCrossItsOWNEmptyChain, aFAULTEDSweepHoldsTheInvariantsAcrossEverySeed, aTakeoverWhoseIMMEDIATEPredecessorIsWHOLLYEMPTYStillSealsTheRealAncestor, aCrossedEpochOPENEDBetweenProbeAndSealBecomesTheAncestor, aCrossedEpochThatOnlyOPENEDIsStillTheAncestor, aRacingChainLONGERThanTheRedriveBudgetStillConverges), matching 'seven tests', and check-tdd PASSED against these bytes, which is what 'each minted red' rests on. The round-1 blocking finding M4.47-R1a the packet still lists as open is the one round 3 measured dead: forcing the seal-loop predicate back to `> 0` reddens the open-only interleave test written for it.
